sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s make your code cleaner and faster with Augmented Assignment Operators! These are like shortcuts for common math operations.

• What augmented assignment operators are (+=, -=, *=, etc.)
• How they make your code shorter and clearer
• When to use them (and when not to!)

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you’re at a lemonade stand. Instead of saying ‘I’ll take my current number of lemons and add 5 more,’ you just say ‘add 5 lemons.’ That’s exactly what augmented assignment operators do!

They combine an operation (like addition) with assignment in one step. For example:
• Instead of `x = x + 2`, you write `x += 2`
• Instead of `total = total * 1.1`, you write `total *= 1.1`

These operators work with all basic math operations:
• `+=` (addition)
• `-=` (subtraction)
• `*=` (multiplication)
• `/=` (division)
• `%=` (remainder)

sections.title: Code Examples
examples:
int x = 10;
x += 5;   // same as x = x + 5  -> 15
x -= 3;   // same as x = x - 3  -> 12
x *= 2;   // same as x = x * 2  -> 24
x /= 4;   // same as x = x / 4  -> 6
x %= 4;   // same as x = x % 4  -> 2

sections.title: Key Points
points: += adds and assigns: x += 5 is equivalent to x = x + 5
-=, *=, /=, %= work similarly for subtraction, multiplication, division, and modulus
Augmented operators are more concise and slightly more efficient
The right-hand expression is evaluated first, then combined with the variable
These operators can be used with any numeric type

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Augmented operators = math + assignment in one step. Most important rule: Right side evaluates first. Practice with counters, totals, and simple updates.
